title: German Aerospace Center (DLR) Researchers Demonstrate Low-Cost Benchmarked-Noise Error Mitigation Across 100-Qubit IBM and IQM Processors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: German Aerospace Center (DLR) researchers demonstrated randomized benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation (bnZNE). It anchors ZNE to error rates measured on classically simulable twin circuits instead of idealized integer folding factors, and improves accuracy without extra shots. Tested on IBM's 156-qubit Heron r2 (ibm_fez) and IQM's 54-qubit Emerald at up to 100 qubits and two-qubit depth 452, it beat standard ZNE on every tested benchmark and showed that circuit depth matters more for mitigation accuracy than circuit area.

themes.theme: Why standard ZNE breaks at utility scale

insights.claim: Standard zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) amplifies noise with redundant gate folds and extrapolates to zero noise, but at utility scale single-qubit gate errors, temporal calibration drift and noise saturation make integer folding factors diverge from physical error rates, introducing systematic bias.
insights.so_what: Standard ZNE results on 100-qubit-scale experiments may carry hidden bias, so treat utility-scale claims that rely on plain ZNE with caution.
insights.quote: single-qubit gate errors, temporal calibration drift, and noise saturation cause the relationship between integer folding factors and physical error rates to diverge, introducing systematic bias
insights.locator: Standard zero-noise extrapolation inflates circuit noise
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: DLR's bnZNE pairs each randomized application circuit with a structure-mirroring twin that keeps the exact physical gate layout but evolves only to a classically computable bitstring or identity state, replacing idealized folding factors (r = 1, 3, 5) with empirically measured error rates.
insights.so_what: Calibrating extrapolation against measured hardware noise is a cheap, generalizable upgrade that any provider's mitigation stack could adopt.
insights.quote: Replaces idealized integer folding factors (r = 1, 3, 5) with empirical error rates ε(r) ∈ [0, 1].
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: bnZNE matches standard ZNE shot budgets: 196,608 total shots per application (32 randomizations x 3 noise levels), with 1,024 shots each for application and benchmark circuits.
insights.so_what: Better accuracy at equal sampling cost means a direct reduction in effective QPU spend per reliable result.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: The bnZNE protocol combines Pauli twirling, dynamical decoupling and twirled readout error extinction (TREX) across multiple randomizations to anchor the extrapolation to real hardware noise conditions.
insights.so_what: This stacks existing mitigation primitives that are already available in IBM's tooling, which lowers adoption friction.
insights.locator: To anchor the classical extrapolation step
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: bnZNE was validated on IBM's 156-qubit Heron r2 (ibm_fez) with a 100-qubit kicked Ising circuit (1,980 CZ gates), 50-qubit QFT and 5-qubit Grover circuits, and on IQM's 54-qubit Emerald with 30-qubit kicked Ising dynamics up to 40 Trotter steps (1,160 CZ gates). Workloads reached two-qubit gate depths up to 452.
insights.so_what: Working across both IBM and IQM gate sets shows the method is vendor-portable, which benefits European hardware like IQM competing with IBM.
insights.locator: IBM Heron r2 Protocol and IQM Emerald Protocol rows
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: DLR's bnZNE outperformed standard ZNE on every tested single-qubit observable and two-qubit correlation-decay benchmark, and the study found that circuit depth plays a stronger role in mitigation accuracy than total circuit area.
insights.so_what: If depth rather than width limits mitigated accuracy, wide-but-shallow circuits are the sweet spot for near-term utility, and hardware roadmaps should prioritize gate fidelity over qubit count.
insights.quote: circuit depth plays a stronger role in mitigation accuracy than total circuit area
insights.locator: To anchor the classical extrapolation step
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: The DLR bnZNE study was supported by the DLR Quantum Computing Initiative (ALQU project), the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, and the European Union's Horizon Europe Q-Neko program.
insights.so_what: German and EU public money is funding vendor-neutral mitigation research that benefits European hardware like IQM.
